html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Tell CI, continuous delivery and continuous deployment apart
  • Explain the GitOps principles, pull versus push and reconciliation
  • Compare recreate, rolling, blue/green, canary, A/B and shadow releases
  • Use Helm charts, releases and values, and Kustomize overlays

2CI, continuous delivery and continuous deployment, the registry, tags and digests

Running case

Harbor Books Ships Every Week

  • A Git repository holds what should run, and every change is a reviewed commit
  • A new storefront goes to a small share of visitors first, and is rolled back if orders drop
  • Staging and production run the same application with different settings
  • In this module you build the delivery path that does all of this

CI, Continuous Delivery and Continuous Deployment Archived topic

  • Continuous integration (CI) merges code changes as often as possible, and ends with a tested artifact
  • Continuous delivery deploys changes automatically to an acceptance environment, with tests and a way to roll back
  • Continuous deployment carries finished software directly to production
  • CI is a prerequisite for CD

Exam tip

CI builds and tests, delivery reaches acceptance, deployment reaches production.

Registry, Tags and Digests

Reference What it means
storefront:stable (a tag) a name that can be moved to point at a different image
storefront@sha256:... (a digest) a hash of the image content: unique to one version and immutable
  • A pipeline builds an image, pushes it to a registry, and the cluster pulls it
  • Deploy by digest when you need the same reference to mean the same image every time
  • Promote the same artifact from test to production, instead of rebuilding it
Exam tip

A tag can move; a digest cannot.

3The OpenGitOps principles, pull versus push, drift and reconciliation, Argo CD and Flux

GitOps: The Four Principles Archived topic

  • Declarative: the desired state is described, not scripted
  • Versioned and immutable: it is stored with a complete history, for example in Git
  • Pulled automatically: software agents pull the desired state from the source
  • Continuously reconciled: agents observe the actual state and keep applying the desired state
  • Git is the usual source of truth; drift, rollback and review all become Git operations
Exam tip

Declarative, versioned and immutable, pulled, continuously reconciled.

Pull, Drift and Reconciliation Archived topic

  • In GitOps the agent pulls the desired state from the source; nothing pushes into the cluster
  • The agent continuously compares the actual state with the desired state
  • Drift is the actual state moving away from the desired state
  • Reconciliation runs whenever there is a divergence, not only on a new commit; traditional CI/CD runs on pre-set triggers

Exam tip

Pull plus continuous reconciliation is what fixes drift.

Argo CD and Flux Archived topic Moving

Tool What it is
Argo CD a GitOps tool for continuous delivery to Kubernetes, with declarative definitions
Flux keeps clusters in sync with sources such as Git repositories and OCI artifacts, and automates updates
  • Both are GitOps tools for Kubernetes: they compare a source with the cluster and bring the cluster into line
  • As of 30 October 2026: Argo, Flux and Helm are CNCF graduated projects
Exam tip

Argo CD and Flux are GitOps tools; Helm is a package manager.

4Recreate, rolling, blue/green, canary, A/B, shadow, progressive delivery with Argo Rollouts

Recreate, Rolling and Blue/Green

  • Recreate: all old Pods are killed first, then the new ones start, so there is downtime
  • Rolling update: Pods are replaced gradually; it is the Deployment default
  • Blue/green: two environments; the idle one is updated and tested, then traffic is switched to it

Exam tip

Recreate has downtime, rolling is gradual, blue/green switches whole environments.

Canary, A/B and Shadow Releases

  • Canary: move traffic gradually to the new version, watch it, then continue or roll back
  • A/B testing: route a set of users, chosen by HTTP headers or cookies, to the new version
  • Shadow (mirroring): copy each request to the new version too, for idempotent requests
  • Canary and A/B need layer 7 traffic control, such as a service mesh or an ingress controller

Exam tip

Canary shifts a share, A/B picks users, shadow copies requests.

Progressive Delivery with Argo Rollouts Beyond the curriculum

Tool What it does
Argo Rollouts a Kubernetes controller and CRDs for blue-green, canary, canary analysis and progressive delivery
Flagger automates canary, A/B, blue/green and mirroring releases with analysis, promotion and rollback
  • Both can work with ingress controllers and service meshes to shift traffic gradually
  • They can read metrics to decide on automatic promotion or rollback
Exam tip

Progressive delivery: shift gradually, measure, then promote or roll back.

5Helm charts, releases and values, Helm commands, Kustomize bases and overlays

Helm: Charts, Releases and Values

  • Helm is the package manager for Kubernetes
  • A chart is a package: Chart.yaml, default values.yaml and templates/
  • A repository collects and shares charts
  • A release is one installed copy of a chart in a cluster; one chart can make many releases
  • Helm merges the chart with values to produce the manifests

Exam tip

Chart plus values makes a release.

Helm in Practice

  • install creates a release from a chart and values, from a -f file or --set
  • upgrade changes a release and updates only what changed
  • history lists the revisions; every install, upgrade or rollback adds one, starting at revision one
  • rollback RELEASE REVISION returns to an earlier revision

Install, upgrade, inspect and roll back a release

helm install shop-db shop/db -f prod.yaml
helm upgrade shop-db shop/db -f prod.yaml
helm history shop-db
helm rollback shop-db 1
helm uninstall shop-db
Exam tip

A rollback adds a new revision; it does not erase the history.

Kustomize: Bases and Overlays

  • Kustomize customizes template-free YAML and leaves the original untouched
  • A base holds the common resources; an overlay adds patches for a variant such as staging or production
  • It is built into kubectl: kubectl kustomize shows the result, kubectl apply -k applies it
  • Helm uses templates and values; Kustomize patches plain YAML

Exam tip

Helm templates; Kustomize patches.

6Promotion across environments, rollback, infrastructure as code, what the exam asks

Promotion, Rollback and Infrastructure as Code Beyond the curriculum

Topic The idea
Promotion the same change moves through the environments, from test to acceptance to production
Rollback helm rollback, kubectl rollout undo, or in GitOps a Git revert that the agent reconciles
Infrastructure as code infrastructure is defined in files, not built by hand, so it is reproducible; Crossplane, a CNCF project, builds control planes for applications and infrastructure
Exam tip

What lives in files and Git can be reviewed, repeated and rolled back.

What the Exam Asks: Application Delivery

  • CI or CD: CI builds and tests; delivery reaches acceptance; deployment reaches production
  • Push or pull: GitOps agents pull the desired state and keep reconciling it
  • Rolling, blue/green or canary: replace gradually, switch whole environments, or shift a share of traffic
  • Helm or Kustomize: templates and values in releases, or patches over a base
  • Tag or digest: a tag can move, a digest cannot
  • Argo CD or Flux, or Helm: GitOps tools, or a package manager
Exam tip

For a delivery question, ask what moves the change: a pipeline, an agent, a package or a patch.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1What is the difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?

  • ADelivery builds the code, and deployment tests it before it is merged
  • BDelivery works for containers in a test setup, and deployment works for virtual machines in production
  • CDelivery reaches an acceptance environment automatically, and deployment goes on to production
  • DDelivery needs a person to approve each step, and deployment skips the tests
Show the answer

Answer: C. Continuous delivery deploys changes automatically into an acceptance environment, with tests and a way to roll back. Continuous deployment carries finished software directly to production. CI is the build and test stage before both.

S2Harbor Books must be sure that staging and production run exactly the same image, even if someone pushes a different image under an existing tag. Which reference does that?

  • AAn image digest, which is a hash of the image content and does not change
  • BThe latest tag, because it points at the image that was tested
  • CThe name of the registry alone, because a registry holds one version
  • DA new tag typed by hand on each node, because tags are checked by the kubelet
Show the answer

Answer: A. A digest identifies one version of an image and is immutable, while a tag can be moved to a different image. The latest tag can move, and a registry holds many images.

S3Which list gives the four GitOps principles of the OpenGitOps project?

  • AImperative, mutable, pushed by hand and checked once a month by an auditor
  • BScripted, versioned, pushed by the pipeline and reconciled only on a new commit
  • CDeclarative, mutable, pulled by hand and compared with the cluster once a week
  • DDeclarative, versioned and immutable, pulled automatically and continuously reconciled
Show the answer

Answer: D. The desired state must be declarative, versioned and immutable, pulled automatically by software agents, and continuously reconciled with the actual state.

S4In GitOps, what does it mean that the desired state is pulled?

  • AA person copies the manifests from Git to the cluster each time a change is reviewed
  • BAn agent fetches the desired state from the source, instead of a pipeline pushing it into the cluster
  • CThe Git server opens a connection to every node and writes the files that changed
  • DThe cluster sends its current state to Git, which then decides what to deploy
Show the answer

Answer: B. Software agents read the desired state from the state store whenever they need to, which makes continuous reconciliation possible. A pushed change happens once, and is not watched afterwards.

S5Someone changes the orders Deployment by hand in a cluster that an Argo CD or Flux agent manages from Git. What should happen?

  • ANothing, because a GitOps agent compares the cluster with Git at installation time
  • BThe agent deletes the Git repository, because the manual change is the new truth
  • CThe agent notices the drift and reconciles the cluster back to the state in Git
  • DThe agent sends the manual change to the other clusters, so that they match
Show the answer

Answer: C. Drift is the actual state moving away from the desired state, and the agent keeps observing the cluster and applies the desired state from Git again. Git stays the source of truth.

S6Which deployment strategy kills all the old Pods before it creates new ones, so that there is downtime?

  • ARolling update, which replaces the Pods gradually while the old ones still serve traffic
  • BRecreate, which stops every old Pod first and then starts the new version
  • CBlue/green, which keeps two environments and switches the traffic between them
  • DCanary, which moves a growing share of the traffic to the new version
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Recreate strategy stops every existing Pod first and only then creates the new ones. The other strategies keep serving users with the old version while the new one comes up.

S7Harbor Books wants to send a small share of visitors to a new storefront version, watch the results, and then increase the share or roll back. Which strategy is this?

  • ACanary, which moves traffic gradually to the new version and allows a quick rollback
  • BRecreate, which replaces the Pods of the whole application at once and accepts a short period of downtime
  • CBlue/green, which switches the traffic from one environment to the other at once
  • DShadow, which copies requests to the new version and does not send real users to it
Show the answer

Answer: A. A canary shifts traffic gradually, so the team can observe the new version in production and roll back if needed. Blue/green switches everything at once, and shadow releases copy requests without serving users from the new version.

S8In Helm, what is a release?

  • AA package of the manifests that an application needs in order to run
  • BA server where charts are collected and shared with other people
  • CA file with the default configuration values that a chart provides
  • DAn instance of a chart that is running in a Kubernetes cluster
Show the answer

Answer: D. A release is a chart installed in a cluster, and the same chart can be installed many times, each as its own release. The package is the chart, the shared collection is a repository, and the defaults live in values.yaml.

S9Which tool customizes plain YAML with a base and overlays, and is built into kubectl?

  • AHelm, which renders templates with values and installs the result as a release in the cluster
  • BFlux, which keeps clusters in sync with sources such as Git repositories
  • CKustomize, which patches template-free YAML and applies it with kubectl apply -k
  • DArgo Rollouts, which adds canary and blue-green releases to Deployments
Show the answer

Answer: C. Kustomize layers overlays with patches over a base of plain YAML, and kubectl can build and apply the result. Helm uses templates, Flux is a GitOps agent, and Argo Rollouts is for progressive delivery.

S10A Helm upgrade of the Harbor Books database release misbehaves. Which command returns to an earlier revision?

  • Ahelm uninstall, which removes the release and its history for good
  • Bhelm rollback with the release name and a revision number
  • Chelm repo add, which registers another chart repository on the client
  • Dhelm search hub, which lists charts found on Artifact Hub
Show the answer

Answer: B. The rollback command takes the release name and a revision and returns the release to that revision, adding a new revision to the history. Uninstall removes the release, and the other commands only deal with repositories and search.

8Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Pipelines CI builds and tests; delivery reaches acceptance; deployment reaches production
Images a tag can move; a digest is a fixed hash
GitOps declarative, versioned and immutable, pulled, continuously reconciled; agents like Argo CD and Flux fix drift
Strategies recreate, rolling, blue/green, canary, A/B and shadow; progressive delivery adds analysis
Helm and Kustomize charts and values make releases; bases and overlays patch YAML
Rollback helm rollback, kubectl rollout undo or a Git revert
